fluff.overview: The Congress-class frigate was one of the Star League Defense Force's most widely produced and longest-serving capital combatants. Commissioned in 2542, the class was designed by Dekirk Aerospace at its Graham IV shipyards and subsequently built by both Dekirk and Challenge Systems of Galax. Classified as a frigate, the Congress combined exceptional speed with heavy capital weaponry in a hull well-suited to independent patrol, convoy escort, fleet screening, and squadron command duties. Fleet commanders valued the design's ability to operate effectively both as part of larger task forces and on independent assignments, a flexibility rare among vessels of its classification. The Congress earned a reputation for punching well above its weight, with many officers regarding it as closer to a light cruiser in practical combat capability than a standard frigate.
fluff.capabilities:
Displacing 760,000 tons and measuring 703 meters, the Congress was capable of three-gravity sustained acceleration with a five-gravity emergency rating. The standard variant's weapons suite centered on twelve Armstrong LN-10 NAC/10 naval autocannons distributed across fore, broadside, and aft quarter batteries, providing consistent kinetic firepower in every engagement geometry. Two Oriente-30 NAC/30 naval autocannons in the aft arc delivered heavy rear-quarter firepower, while a nose-mounted Killer Whale and two broadside White Shark capital missile launchers provided long-range striking power. Four Magna large lasers supplemented the broadside and aft quarter batteries. The hull incorporated endo steel construction and 487 tons of Blue Nose 440CL ferro-carbide armor, with three GM 8050 Starlifter engines providing the class's exceptional thrust. Vargas 5T communications and Wolf 157 targeting systems coordinated fire control, while a KF Mark XXV jump drive supported fleet operations. Two DropShip docking collars, six fighter bays, and four small craft bays supported organic aerospace and transport operations. The armor allocation concerned some fleet officers, who considered it light for a vessel mounting this level of armament, though the Congress's speed served as adequate compensation.

The Clan refit, undertaken around 2914, added a lithium-fusion battery for rapid successive jumps, HarJel hull sealant for improved damage control, and ER large lasers replacing the standard energy weapons, while expanding fighter capacity to ten bays with five small craft bays. Armor was reduced to 433 tons of ferro-carbide. The Congress-D variant replaced forward NAC/10 batteries with NAC/30 naval autocannons, increasing forward engagement power at the cost of reduced sensor capability.
fluff.deployment: The Congress served as a backbone escort and independent patrol vessel throughout the SLDF fleet. The SLS Rickover was lost in 2572 during the United Triumph Military Exercises when a catastrophic collision with the SLS Davion's Heart destroyed both vessels, one of the earliest recorded WarShip losses in peacetime fleet operations. The SLS Star Devil was destroyed during the Periphery Uprising near Brisbane after engaging a Taurian convoy, destroying three of four Lola II-class destroyers before being overwhelmed by concentrated fire. The SLS Europa held the grim distinction of being the first WarShip lost during Operation LIBERATION, destroyed on January 23, 2777, as part of Task Force Leonidas. The SLS Admiral Perry led the Draconis Rift Squadron in 2764, while the SLS Anchorage served as flagship of the SLDF 17th Fleet, demonstrating the class's suitability for command roles. After the Star League's collapse, Congress frigates served across the Successor States. The DCS Halland and DCS Stockholm were both destroyed at Imbrial III in early 2790, while the CCS Tianjin survived an ambush at Corey in September 2787.
fluff.history:
The Congress-class frigate was born from one of the most scandalous episodes in Star League-era defense contracting. Dekirk Aerospace designed the vessel at its Graham IV shipyards in the mid-twenty-sixth century, creating a fast and heavily armed frigate that combined the firepower expected of a much larger vessel with exceptional speed for its displacement. Challenge Systems of Galax, however, began producing the same design after 2540 following an espionage operation that resulted in a landmark lawsuit. The legal controversy became one of the era's most notorious cases of industrial theft in the defense sector. Despite the scandal, both yards continued production, eventually laying down approximately 200 keels between them. Challenge Systems also produced the Congress-D, a dedicated Federated Suns variant that enhanced forward engagement power at the cost of sensor fidelity, as the Hegemony-grade electronics could not be reproduced to original specifications.

The Congress saw extensive combat from its earliest years of service. One vessel was lost during peacetime fleet exercises in 2572 after a catastrophic collision, while another was destroyed during the Periphery Uprising after engaging a Taurian convoy and accounting for three enemy destroyers before being overwhelmed. During Operation LIBERATION, a Congress became the first WarShip lost in Task Force Leonidas's assault on the Caspar drone network defending Terra. After the fall of the Star League, Congress frigates served in virtually every Successor State navy and with ComStar. The class's combination of speed and firepower made these vessels valuable assets in fleets that could no longer replace WarShip losses, and individual vessels saw action across multiple theaters during the Succession Wars.

Congress frigates that survived the Exodus were subsequently modernized by the Clans around 2914, producing a capable refit that served across virtually every Clan touman. The Jihad consumed many of the surviving vessels on both sides of the conflict. Wolf's Dragoons, ComStar, and multiple Clans lost Congress frigates during engagements ranging from Mars to Dyev, while Blakist Caspar II drones accounted for at least one Clan vessel during Operation SCOUR. Despite centuries of attrition, the design proved remarkably durable. At least two Congress frigates remained operational through 3145, serving in Clan Wolf and Clan Snow Raven naval formations, evidence of a design whose combat effectiveness endured across six centuries of service.
